title: Compare bonds before rotating
statement:
Around which bond in CH₃–CH=CH₂ can the molecule rotate without losing a pi overlap?

[_]{a}

choices: The bond connecting CH₃ to CH
explanations: It is an ordinary single bond.
Twisting it weakens the side-on overlap.
The double bond has the higher rotational barrier.

hints: The carbon skeleton contains one C–C single and one C=C double bond.
A double bond includes an aligned p-orbital overlap.
Rotation about the single bond preserves that overlap.
solution: The carbon skeleton contains one C–C single and one C=C double bond. A double bond includes an aligned p-orbital overlap. Rotation about the single bond preserves that overlap. It is an ordinary single bond.
